### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every case followed the same route: A38 → A14 → A15, then either A20 → A21 (about 50 in 100 cases) or A22 (about 50 in 100), then A23. A38's only observed successor was A14, and A23 followed A38 four to five steps later, in roughly equal shares. [DIR001, LAG001, REL001, REL012, REL013, REL019]
- In the later window, about 48 in 100 cases go directly from A38 to A23, one step apart, skipping A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 entirely. A38's outgoing transitions split about 52% to A14 and 48% to A23, whereas no direct A38→A23 step was observed in the earlier window. [DIR001, LAG001, REL005, REL006]
- Participation of the bypassed activities fell accordingly: A14 and A15 from all 200 traces to about 105 in 200 (about 53 in 100), A20 and A21 from about 50 to 29 in 100, and A22 from about 50 to 24 in 100. A20 and A22 remain mutually exclusive alternatives, and in about 48 in 100 later cases neither appears. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL013, REL016]
- When the full route is still taken, its internal order is unchanged: A38 before A14, A14 before A15, A20 before A21, and A23 last. [REL001, REL006, REL012, REL014]
- Relative positions shifted mildly and consistently with more short traces: A23 now occurs earlier within cases (mean position about 0.44 → 0.41, with more spread), A38 slightly later (about 0.30 → 0.32). [POS001, POS002]
- Elapsed time between consecutive completions changed on three activity pairs: A38→A14 grew from about 2.0 to about 3.0 hours in the cases still containing that step, A28→A34 fell from about 0.9 to about 0.45 hours, and A35→A34 from about 0.20 to about 0.08 hours. [TWAIT003, TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that in the later window a shortcut is taken in roughly half of the cases: about 48 in 100 executions go directly from A38 to A23, bypassing A14, A15 and the alternative segment A20→A21 / A22, which in the earlier window were executed in every case. This is shown directly by the successor change at A38 (previously 100% to A14, now about 52/48), by A38 and A23 appearing one step apart in about 48 in 100 later cases (never in the earlier window), and by A23 and A38 appearing without A14 in about 48 in 100 later cases; the participation drops match the same split, and the order of the retained route is unchanged. The volume of qualifying items also far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 29 control-flow items against about 0.45 expected by chance, and 3 time items against about 0.01. [DIR001, LAG001, REL005, REL006, OCC001, OCC005, screening]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether the direct A38→A23 route existed at a very low rate before (it was not observed in 200 earlier traces, so a rare pre-existing path cannot be fully excluded), nor why cases take one route or the other. Several items describe the same underlying split and are not independent confirmations. [DIR001, LAG001, OCC001]

Other differences: timing changed beyond the routing split itself — the gap from A38 to A14 lengthened by about 1 hour in the cases that still take that step, and the gaps A28→A34 and A35→A34 shortened to roughly half or less; these elapsed-time changes (which measure time between consecutive completions, not pure waiting or service time) are not explained by the bypass hypothesis. [TWAIT003, TWAIT001, TWAIT002]
